name: Scanduro Connect: QR Codes and Menus
author: scanduro

sections.description:
Scanduro Connect brings dynamic QR code creation and management to WordPress. Create a QR code for a published page or post, display it on your website, or download a PNG for print. Update an eligible QR code’s destination later without replacing the printed code.

QR codes for your WordPress website

  • Create a dynamic QR code for a published WordPress page or post.
  • Choose an existing QR code from your Scanduro workspace or import it by ID.
  • Download a 1024-pixel PNG QR image for posters, flyers, signs and table cards.
  • Display saved QR codes with the Scanduro QR Code block or a shortcode.
  • Change an eligible dynamic QR code’s destination when your content moves.

Restaurant menu and ordering links

Add a button linking to your published Scanduro menu or ordering page using the Scanduro Menu or Order Link block or shortcode. Visitors open your hosted Scanduro page while you keep your existing WordPress website.

Account and pricing

Account-connected QR management requires a Scanduro account on a plan with live API access (currently Pro and above). The connector itself is free to install. Manually configured menu/ordering buttons need no API connection; the linked service remains subject to its own Scanduro plan and availability.

This is not a WooCommerce sync tool, payment gateway, embedded checkout or independent QR hosting service.

External service and privacy

This plugin connects to https://scanduro.com/api/v1 only after an administrator explicitly connects an API key or requests an operation. It sends the key in an HTTPS Authorization header to verify the connection and manage the selected codes. Creating a QR sends the selected published page’s title and permalink. Updating a code sends the new destination. Rendering a QR sends its canonical short URL to the Scanduro image-rendering endpoint.

Account/key information, QR IDs, destinations and images are returned to WordPress. QR images are cached in the site’s public uploads folder. Normal visitor page loads do not call the authenticated API. Following a link or scanning its image visits Scanduro’s resolver or hosted page under the service’s privacy terms.

The API key is stored in a non-autoloaded WordPress option. Administrators and parties with database/server access can access stored credentials. Protect database backups and revoke the key in Scanduro if compromised. Disconnecting removes the saved key. Uninstalling removes plugin settings/mappings; remote QR codes and uploaded PNGs are intentionally preserved to avoid breaking existing printed or directly embedded links.

sections.installation:
1. Install and activate

You need administrator access to a WordPress website running WordPress 6.5 or later and PHP 7.4 or later.

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, open Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for Scanduro Connect and choose Scanduro Connect: QR Codes and Menus by scanduro.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Alternatively, download the ZIP from this listing, open Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin, select the ZIP, click Install Now, and activate it.

2. Connect Scanduro for QR management

Creating, importing and updating QR codes requires a Scanduro workspace with live API access, currently Pro or above. The WordPress plugin is free to install. If you only want a menu or ordering button, skip to section 4.

  1. Sign in to Scanduro and open API Keys.
  2. Create a dedicated live API key with codes:read and codes:write permissions for this WordPress website.
  3. In WordPress, open Settings > Scanduro Connect.
  4. Paste the key into Connect or replace live API key, then click Connect Scanduro.
  5. Check that the page shows Connected key: with your key’s name.

Use an API key, not your Scanduro password or a sandbox key. Keep the key private.

3. Create or display a QR code

  1. Publish the page or post you want visitors to open. It must be public and not password-protected.
  2. In Settings > Scanduro Connect, under Create a QR for a published page, select it from Page or post and click Create or retrieve this page’s QR.
  3. Find the result under Saved QR codes. Use Download PNG for a printable image.
  4. To display it on your website, copy its shortcode into a WordPress Shortcode block. Alternatively, add the Scanduro QR Code block and paste the saved code’s ID into Saved QR ID.
  5. Publish or update the WordPress page, view it as a visitor, and scan the QR with your phone to confirm it opens the intended destination.

To use a QR you already have, click Load QR list, choose it from Existing QR, and click Save selected QR. You can also enter its ID in Or enter a QR ID and click Save QR by ID. IDs start with lnk_; they are not the destination URL.

To change an eligible code later, use Update a destination, enter its QR ID and New destination, and click Change destination. Scan the same printed QR afterward to verify the change. Table-ordering codes have protected destinations.

4. Add a menu or ordering button

This button does not require an API key. You still need a published Scanduro menu or ordering page, subject to its Scanduro plan and availability.

  1. Edit the WordPress page where you want the button.
  2. Add the Scanduro Menu or Order Link block.
  3. Paste your published link into Scanduro menu or ordering URL, then choose the Link text, such as View menu or Order now.
  4. Publish or update the page and test the button as a visitor.

Use an HTTPS Scanduro link on scanduro.com, scanduro.page or scandu.ro (including supported scanduro.page and scandu.ro subdomains). This version does not accept your own custom domain for the menu button. It opens the hosted page; it does not embed a menu or checkout.
sections.faq:
Is a paid Scanduro plan required?

Live account-connected QR management currently requires Pro or above. The plugin does not unlock API access on Free or Starter. A manually configured menu/ordering link does not need an API connection.

Does this process guest payments?

No. Menu and ordering buttons open the existing hosted Scanduro flow. This plugin does not handle card details, refunds or settlement.

What happens if I disconnect?

The key is removed and new API operations stop. Cached QR displays remain available, and existing printed Scanduro codes are not deleted.

Why cannot I repoint a table QR?

Table-ordering codes have protected destinations. Repointing one would send seated guests to the wrong place. Only ordinary dynamic URL codes can be updated through this connector.

What if a create request times out?

Retry the same page request. Its identity and original inputs are retained. Requests older than 23 hours are refused rather than risking a duplicate after API replay storage expires. If a request remains locked after a server crash, contact support to reconcile it; do not delete its mapping to force creation.

Does a dynamic QR preserve an unpublished WordPress page?

No. The stable QR URL and the destination website have separate lifecycles. Keep the destination published or explicitly point the code at another valid destination.

Are QR codes created automatically on every post save?

No. Creation and destination changes are explicit administrator actions.

Which shortcodes are available?

[scanduro_qr id=”lnk_YOUR_ID” label=”Open link”]
[scanduro_link url=”https://scanduro.page/your-menu” label=”View menu”]

Initial release: API connection, create/import/update dynamic URL QR codes, cached PNG assets, QR and menu/order blocks and shortcodes.
